title: KV transform sparsity + bitpacking field study: HBST (hybrid bitpack-sparse transform)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Run a set of targeted field experiments that combine light-weight lossy transforms (local sparsity projection) with tight bit-packing to reduce GPU KV cache resident memory. Evaluate HBST (hybrid bitpack-sparse transform) across FP8/INT8/INT4 profiles and measure downstream quality, latency and memory savings when used with continuous batching and prefix caching.
motivation: Hosted and Dedicated customers are hitting limits on GPU memory for long-context workloads. Prior work explored pure quantization or blockwise compaction; HBST aims to trade small, recoverable quality loss for larger memory reductions when combined with batching and selective resident set eviction policies.
hypothesis: Applying a two-stage transform (light sparsity projection followed by adaptive bitpacking tuned per-layer and per-cohort) will reduce KV resident memory by 30-60% with <2% relative degradation on generation quality metrics for most customer cohorts. For extreme low-bit modes (INT4), targeted per-token fidelity retention (hot-token keep) will reduce regressions to <5%.
experiment_plan: 1) Implement HBST encoder/decoder in runtime-memory branch. 2) Add per-token hotness scoring hook in serving runtime to decide keep/evict at encode-time. 3) Run lab microbenchmarks on representative models (Llama-2-13B, mix-architectures) with synthetic and real workload traces. 4) Run A/B traffic (shadow + canary) on dedicated pool using 5 customer-like workload cohorts. 5) Collect quality signals (perplexity on held prompts, token-level next-token accuracy, rouge/meteor for summarization prompts), latency and p50/p95/p99 metrics, and memory footprint per-GPU. 6) Iterate quant profiles and per-layer thresholds. 7) Produce rollout playbook if results meet acceptance criteria.
datasets:
- Synthetic long-context traces derived from internal eval corpus (longform-dialogue, codegen traces).
- Production-sampled anonymous traces from three workload cohorts (chat-heavy, retrieval-augmented, summarization).
- PRD prompt set: drive/redwood/evals/HBST/seed_prompts-2026-02-05.csv
metrics:
- Memory reduction: resident KV bytes per GPU (absolute and %).
- Quality: delta perplexity, relative MRR on next-token, NLG metrics for prompts (ROUGE-L, BLEU where applicable), and human-rate-quality on a 500-sample blind set.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 generation token latency and end-to-end response latency under continuous batching.
- Cost: estimated token-cost change and GPU utilization.
- Failure modes: fraction of requests requiring fallback to full-fidelity cache and rate of hallucination spike events.
acceptance_criteria:
- Achieve >=30% median KV memory reduction with p95 >=25% across test cohorts.
- Quality regressions: median delta perplexity <2%, human blind-review regression <=3% across safe prompts.
- Latency change: p95 token latency increase <=5ms when using HBST under standard batching settings.
- Fallbacks triggered <1% of requests and automatic fallback path performs under SLA.
- No data integrity/serialization bugs in HBST decoder in stress runs.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Lab validation on isolated cluster. Phase 1: Shadow deployment on dedicated pool for 72h with real traffic samples. Phase 2: Canary rollout (5% of live traffic) with circuit breaker monitoring. Phase 3: Incremental expansion to 25% then 100% on dedicated lane only. For Hosted: only enable as an opt-in model variant behind quota and opt-in feature flag. Must include automated rollback on quality or latency regressions.
monitoring_and_alerts:
- Add HBST-specific metrics: encode_time_ms, decode_time_ms, residual_error_distribution, fallback_rate, hot_token_keep_ratio.
- Dashboard: runtime->HBST->per-model and per-cohort panels.
- Alerts: fallback_rate > 0.5% in 5m window; median decode_time > 10ms; human-blind-sample drift detected by regression alert.
- Integrations: trace links to console traces and SLO incidents. Dashboards: grafana/runtime/HBST and internal BigQuery job hb_study_exports.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Quality regressions for rare cohorts: mitigate with cohort-aware conservative thresholds and automatic per-cohort disable.
- CPU overhead for encode/decode: offload to asynchronous worker threads and quantify overhead; fall back to pure quant profile if CPU budget exceeded.
- Serialization incompatibilities: use versioned on-disk format and backward-compatible decoder.
- Operational complexity: provide a single feature flag to disable HBST globally and per-project.
